presentingComplaint: Sudden-onset sore throat and fever for 2 days
history: Previously well 14-year-old schoolgirl with 2 days of abrupt sore throat, pain on swallowing, and fever up to 39°C. Reports headache and mild odynophagia. Notably NO cough, NO rhinorrhoea, and NO hoarseness. Two classmates recently had similar sore-throat illness. No known drug allergy. No prior rheumatic fever, no significant PMH.
examination: Ill-appearing but not toxic. Oropharynx shows erythematous, swollen tonsils with patchy white-yellow tonsillar exudate. Tender, enlarged anterior cervical lymph nodes bilaterally. No conjunctival injection, no coryza, no cough during consult. No rash, no strawberry tongue at present. Chest clear. Abdomen soft, no hepatosplenomegaly.
microbiology: Throat swab RADT positive for GAS; culture pending (confirmatory, not required before treatment when RADT positive)
citations: Harrison 22e — Pharyngitis, Sinusitis, Otitis, and Other Upper Respiratory Tract Infections
stewardship: Oral penicillin V 500 mg BD (or amoxicillin 500 mg BD) for 10 days — first-line for confirmed GAS pharyngitis to eradicate organism and prevent acute rheumatic fever. Narrow-spectrum penicillin remains drug of choice; no documented GAS penicillin resistance.
contraindications: Penicillin/beta-lactam allergy — use a macrolide (azithromycin) or first-generation cephalosporin (if non-anaphylactic)
Avoid amoxicillin/ampicillin empirically if infectious mononucleosis is possible (morbilliform rash risk)
edgeCases: Centor/McIsaac score of 4 (tonsillar exudate, tender anterior nodes, fever, no cough, age <15) supports testing and treatment
Scarlet fever if sandpaper rash + strawberry tongue develops
Missed peritonsillar abscess if trismus, uvular deviation or 'hot-potato' voice appears
expectedMaiK: Classic bacterial (Group A strep) pharyngitis with high Centor/McIsaac score and positive RADT — treat with narrow-spectrum penicillin to prevent rheumatic fever; do not use empiric antibiotics for low-probability viral sore throat.
expectedNextQuestions: Any penicillin or other drug allergy?
Presence of cough, coryza or hoarseness (suggesting viral cause)?
Any prior rheumatic fever or recent streptococcal contact?
expectedInvestigations: Rapid antigen detection test (RADT) for Group A Streptococcus
Throat culture if RADT negative in a child/adolescent
Monospot / EBV serology if mononucleosis suspected
